name: Mirage Console — Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector
thesis: Every reference tool (LangSmith, Langfuse, Phoenix, Jaeger, DevTools) stops the trace at what the tool wrapper *logged* — model-reported args. Mirage sits between reasoning and the data plane, so it records the real OpRecord (exact path, exact bytes, the mount/source that served it, cache hit vs fetch, latency, content fingerprint/revision) at the chokepoint inside every backend read/write. The Console makes that the bottom of the tree: a run renders as a Chrome-DevTools-Network-style waterfall over the one canonical spine — Session › Run › Step › {Reasoning | ToolCall} › VfsOp — with a synchronized inspector that, on selecting any span, shows reasoning, command, untruncated args/result, AND the ground-truth data-plane effects. It wins for debugging because it answers the one question output-only evaluators structurally cannot: not "what did the agent say it read," but "what bytes did it actually touch, served from where, at what cost, and which reasoning step caused this write." A Run is a first-class, listable, filterable, permalinkable, immutable noun; the Span tree, ScoreCard, and relay feed fold ONTO it by key rather than living as parallel worlds; and governance (effect class, reversibility) rides as a decoration on the spine, surfaced when a write touches a system of record — never a permanent modal-and-counter tax.
paradigm: Trace Waterfall + Correlated Inspector (distributed-tracing span waterfall fused with Chrome DevTools Network panel). Left rail = run list (the Network "requests" equivalent, but each row is a whole run). Center = time-ordered waterfall of spans with duration bars on a shared time axis; the deepest lane is the VfsOp data-plane layer. Right = a docked inspector that reacts to selection — reasoning, command, args/result, and per-op ground truth (bytes/mount/source/cache/fingerprint/revision/latency-phases/effect-class). A persistent scrub cursor over the waterfall reconstructs VFS/overlay/pending-effect state at step N. Live runs stream into the exact same view and freeze into an immutable artifact on RUN_FINISHED — one mental model, no live-vs-replay split.
informationArchitecture:
Top-level nav replaces the current verb-keyed `Workspaces / Run / Trajectory / State / Promote` (all siblings scoped to one `consoleStore.activeId`) with object-keyed routes where the Run/Trace is the spine:

  • Runs  (default) — /runs : the cross-session run index. List + filter + search over every run that ever executed; this is the home and the thing "review existing interactions" lands on.
  • Trace  — /runs/:runId : the waterfall + inspector for one run (permalinkable; /runs/:runId/step/:stepId deep-links one span). THE primary screen.
  • Compare — /runs/compare?a=&b= : side-by-side run diff (waterfall + ScoreCard + rollups).
  • Workspaces — /workspaces : the build-and-branch surface (the *old* console, demoted to where it belongs — creating a workspace is one way to *create* runs, not the center of gravity).
  • Live — /live : the relay firehose (old TracesView), an optional raw seq-ordered cross-session tail, explicitly secondary.

The object hierarchy as navigated (the one canonical spine, every other tree folded onto it by key):
  Session (== AG-UI thread_id; optional Investigation envelope; backed by a ConsoleWorkspace branch)
    └─ Run (run-{uuid}; the trace root; terminal RUN_FINISHED/RUN_ERROR) ── joins by run_id to: ScoreCard overlay · forensic Span tree · relay StreamEvents
        └─ Step (step-N; holds reasoning + message_id + tool_call_ids[])
            ├─ Reasoning (THINKING_*/TEXT_* folded into step.reasoning / MessageBlock)
            └─ ToolCall (tc-{uuid}; tool_name 'exec'; args=raw shell; result=stdout+exit_code; == exactly one Workspace.execute())
                └─ VfsOp (OpRecord: op/path/source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix/fingerprint/revision/is_cache) ── THE differentiating leaf
                    └─ decorations: EffectClass · CaptureState · Cache/Latency phase · [Lineage edge · PolicyDecision — reserved slots]

How a user moves list → run → detail: In Runs, a user scans rows (prompt, status, error, model, cost, tokens, wallclock, op count, bytes r/w, cache-hit-rate, touched-mount chips) and filters by any of those. Clicking a row routes to /runs/:runId and renders the waterfall: rows are Steps, each expandable to its ToolCall(s), each expandable to its VfsOp children, all on one shared horizontal time axis with duration bars. Selecting any span populates the right Inspector with the payload for that level — a Step shows reasoning + said-to-user; a ToolCall shows command + untruncated stdout + exit_code; a VfsOp shows the full ground-truth record. Hovering a Step highlights its bytes in the data lane and vice-versa (wiring the dead onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId hooks). A "jump to cause" affordance on any VfsOp selects the ToolCall and Step that produced it. The scrub cursor at the top reconstructs filesystem/overlay/pending-effect state at that point. The Eval and State tabs of the inspector hang ScoreCard and OverlayDiff off the same selected run by run_id.

signatureInteractions: Scrub the data plane (not just the chat): a single cursor on the top track reconstructs the VFS/overlay/pending-effects state at step N — drag it and the State inspector + effect counts update to that moment, using mirage's OverlayDiff + snapshots + fingerprints. Borrowed from Redux DevTools / rrweb, but over real filesystem state, where Langfuse 'session replay' can only re-render text turns.

Hover-correlate reasoning ↔ bytes: hovering a Step highlights exactly the VfsOp rows it caused (and dims the rest); hovering a VfsOp highlights its owning ToolCall and Step. This finally wires the onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId hooks that StepCard/RunTracePanel already expose but RunPage passes none of — answering 'which reasoning step caused this write?', which is structurally unanswerable in the current UI.

Jump-to-cause from a VfsOp: any data-plane op has a 'caused by' affordance that selects the exact ToolCall and Step that produced it — real causal edges via the stamped tool_call_id on each OpRecord, not timestamp-window bucketing. 'Caused-by' is rendered distinctly from 'happened-after' (solid connector vs faint chronology).

Latency phase decomposition on every bar: each Step/ToolCall duration bar is segmented into model-time | cache-lookup | byte-fetch | vfs-other, computed from per-op duration_ms + the Span cache_hits/api_calls/misses metrics. Click a slow bar → the Inspector donut tells you whether to fix the prompt (model-time heavy), the data layout (byte-fetch heavy), or the cache (many cache-misses). No competitor has phase-level data-layer timing.

Drift / stale-data flag in the VfsOp inspector: when a read's pinned revision/fingerprint differs from the current backend revision, the op is flagged 'read v3; current v5'. This expresses a class of bug — 'the agent pulled stale data' — that output-only evaluators cannot represent, because only mirage observed the ETag/VersionId at read time.

Filter + permalink the firehose into the spine: cross-session search ('every run that wrote to /slack') in Runs, and a per-step permalink (/runs/:runId/step/:stepId) that opens the exact selected span in an immutable, shareable state.
leveragesMirageData: "The whole design is built so the bottom of the tree is verified bytes from the governed data plane — the one thing a runtime-internal tool can do and external wrappers cannot. (1) Data-plane span layer beneath every tool call: the VfsOp lane renders the real OpRecord (record.py: op/path/source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix/fingerprint/revision, derived is_cache) as the leaf of every exec ToolCall — a DevTools-network waterfall over actual I/O, not model-reported args. This requires the brief's central fix: return exec_node.records from execute() (ExecutionNode.records IS the exact per-execute op set) and stamp tool_call_id/step_id/run_id on each CUSTOM vfs_op at emission (server.py L1401-1411 currently emits only op/path/bytes/mount_prefix), then fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer (NULL today) — collapsing the three incompatible correlation schemes into the spine. (2) Data-correctness debugging: the VfsOp inspector surfaces fingerprint(ETag/md5) and revision(VersionId/SHA), enabling the 'read the wrong file / pulled stale data' drift flag — a bug class output-only evaluators can't express. (3) True latency attribution: phase-segmented bars use per-op duration_ms plus the Span layer's SpanMetrics (api_calls, cache_hits, cache_misses; span.py) — the only place those are aggregated — to split model vs cache-lookup vs byte-fetch, and to reconstruct cache HITS that emit no OpRecord (derive from is_cache==ram / absence of a network op / Span cache_hits). (4) Effect-class + reversibility governance on real writes: because mirage sees the write and the mount, the Effects tab classifies each write (scratch/durable-internal/system-of-record/external-effect via the _EFFECT_BY_PREFIX map) with reversibility and ties it to the causing Step — flagging system-of-record and irreversible external effects, honestly labeling capture_state=simulated rather than dressing the no-op promote (console_promote hardcodes simulated:true, server.py L2746-2761) as a guarded action. (5) Real time-travel over state: the scrub cursor + before/after content diff use OverlayDiff + snapshots + fingerprints to show what a captured write actually changed. Run-level rollups (bytes r/w, cache-hit-rate, tokens, cost) come from the Span metrics and the ScoreCard joined by run_id, not ad-hoc client recompute; the forensic Span tree (currently a 20-command demo with agent_id='demo-agent', consumed by no UI) becomes the waterfall's metric backbone once real session_id/run_id are wired into TracingWorkspace's spans."
fixesCurrentConsole: "Maps 1:1 to the six evidenced critiques. (1) 'No run/trace noun — Run is a verb (a chat box)': the Runs index makes Run a first-class, listable, filterable, permalinkable object at /runs and the IA's spine root; 'chat at an agent' moves into the demoted Workspaces screen as merely one way to *create* a run. (2) 'Cannot review past runs — RunPage nulls sessionId on every workspace switch and never calls listSessions()': the Runs index calls listSessions()/getSessionTrace() (which already exist and power the other platform) and routes by run_id; reviewing a run never re-runs it and never resets a workspace out from under you — runs are immutable artifacts persisted in the store, not a 2000-event RAM ring or localStorage. (3) 'Reasoning↔data correlation built and dead — RunPage passes none of onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId': the Trace screen wires all three for hover-correlate and click-to-inspect, plus a jump-to-cause edge. (4) 'Correlation is timestamp-guessed and buggy (non-breaking loop at correlateEvents.ts L34-39; session leak; orphaned ops)': we replace timestamp bucketing with the stamped tool_call_id on every VfsOp (the brief's NEEDS-PLUMBING fix), so ops attach to their exact ToolCall/Step — no last-match bug, no cross-session leak, no dropped post-step orphans. (5) 'Governance theater drowns the signal and the theater is fake (persistent pending counter, Promote tab, LIVE red-chrome, simulated promote)': the global pending-effects counter and global LIVE chrome are removed; effect class/reversibility become per-write decorations in the Inspector's Effects tab surfaced only when relevant; TEST/LIVE is scoped to a workspace; and 'commit' is explicitly separated from 'review' with an honest SIMULATED banner instead of a guarded modal for a no-op. (6) 'No diff, no scrub, no search, mutable evidence; ignores reusable trace infra': we add a real before/after content diff (State tab), a scrub cursor over data-plane state, full-text cross-run search + per-step permalinks, and we build directly on the ignored infra — RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock, listTraces/getTrace/getSessionTrace, the Span tree at /api/traces, and replayAguiEvents — instead of reinventing a weaker write-focused subset; the immutable frozen artifact makes the record un-erasable (no destructive Reset on the review path)."
risks: The headline differentiator (VfsOp → ToolCall causal edges, drift flags, jump-to-cause) is dark until the NEEDS-PLUMBING fix ships: return exec_node.records and stamp tool_call_id/step_id/run_id at emission, then fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer. Until then the waterfall must fall back to the buggy timestamp correlation and honestly label op→step attribution as 'inferred', which weakens the core promise.

fingerprint/revision/source/duration_ms are dropped today at the JSONL boundary, the CUSTOM vfs_op value, and from_op_record. The VfsOp ground-truth card and drift flag are empty until all three paths copy these fields — and they must agree, or the inspector shows contradictory data.

The forensic Span tree (the metric backbone for rollups + latency phases) is a 20-command demo with agent_id='demo-agent' and no real session join; latency decomposition and accurate cost/cache rollups depend on wiring real session_id/run_id into TracingWorkspace spans, which is non-trivial and may lag the UI.

Cache HITS emit no OpRecord (dispatch short-circuits before record()), so the byte-fetch-vs-cache phase split and cache-hit-rate must be reconstructed from is_cache/absence-of-network-op/Span cache_hits — a heuristic that can be wrong and must be labeled as derived, not measured.

ScoreCard join is convention-only (RunArtifacts.session_id == session id; no enforced FK from scorecards.run_id), and the platform never triggers a sweep — the Eval tab will read 'not scored' for most live runs until evals are joined and triggerable.

VFS browse/content-diff is string-parsed ls -la/cat (brittle on spaces/sizes, text-only, no real mtime/pagination); before/after diffs of binary or large files will be lossy or fail and need a structured FS read to be trustworthy.

Scale: large runs (hundreds of ops, long outputs) demand virtualization, server-side pagination, and standardizing on the arcadia_store (which currently degrades silently to RAM); a naive waterfall over the localStorage/RAM-ring path will jank or lose data on exactly the big runs people most need to debug.

tool_name is always 'exec' with a raw shell-string arg, so read/write/external intent cannot be read off the tool schema — every classification (effect class, kind) must be derived from the VfsOp/mount layer; if that derivation is wrong, the governance flags mislead.

lineage/policy/credential/PII panels are reserved 'not-yet-emitted' slots; if they read as broken-empty rather than deliberately-pending, they undercut trust — they must be visibly marked roadmap, not faked.

name: Mirage Time Machine
thesis: Every other agent trace viewer is a transcript reader: it plays back what the model *said* it did. Mirage is the only runtime that sits on the data-plane chokepoint (observe.context.record() inside every backend read/write), so the bottom of its tree is verified bytes, not model claims. The Mirage Time Machine makes TIME the spine: one global scrubber steps through a run event-by-event, and at every cursor position the screen shows three reconstructed-to-that-instant truths side by side — the agent's reasoning (what it was thinking), the in-flight tool call (what it claimed to do), and the actual VFS/world state (what it really read/wrote, what was mounted, what bytes existed). The killer move is the third panel: a Redux-DevTools/rr/rrweb scrubber over a *governed data plane* rather than over DOM or chat text, made real by mirage's OpRecord stream + OverlayDiff + snapshots + content fingerprints. You scrub to step 7, see the reasoning say "reading the latest invoice," and watch the data panel reveal it actually read a stale revision (md5 mismatch vs HEAD) from a cache hit — a data-correctness bug that output-only evaluators structurally cannot express. Breakpoints (on error, policy-deny, write-to-system-of-record, fingerprint-drift) let you hit play and auto-stop at the moment it went wrong, then step backward one event at a time to find the cause. It wins for debugging because it collapses "model mistake vs data mistake" into a single scrub, and because a run is a first-class immutable artifact you reopen and share a permalink to one exact tick — never a chat you have to re-run.
paradigm: Time-Travel Replay Debugger. The product is organized around a monotonic event cursor (a tick index into the run's ordered AG-UI + VfsOp event log) rather than around a chat or a workspace. The persistent spine is a global transport bar (step-back / play / pause / step-forward / speed, plus a draggable timeline scrubber) pinned to the bottom of every run view, exactly like rr's reverse-execution controls or Redux DevTools' action slider, but extended with rrweb-style state reconstruction. Setting the cursor to tick N is a pure function over the immutable event log: it replays events [0..N] through the existing aguiEventReducer to reconstruct agent/reasoning/tool state, and replays the VfsOp subsequence to reconstruct the data-plane state (which mounts existed, what had been read, the overlay's captured writes so far, pending effects so far). Three coordinated panels re-render to that instant. Breakpoints are predicates over the event stream (error, exit_code!=0, policy-deny [reserved], op.effect_class=='system-of-record', write to external-effect, fingerprint/revision drift, path glob, bytes>threshold); Play advances until the next matching tick and halts. Everything is causality-aware: because we stamp tool_call_id on every VfsOp at emission, "this reasoning step caused this write" is a real edge, not a timestamp guess — so the debugger can do true reverse-step "jump to the cause of this byte" rather than mere chronological rewind.
informationArchitecture:
TOP-LEVEL NAV (left rail, persistent): (1) Runs — the home; a filterable, searchable, permalinkable list of all runs across all sessions [the noun that today does not exist]. (2) Live — runs currently streaming, which seamlessly become frozen artifacts in Runs on completion (one view, no live-vs-replay mental split). (3) Compare — pick 2+ runs, diff their traces/scorecards/state. (4) Library — saved breakpoint sets, exported runs, permalinks. (5) Moat (clearly-labeled "reserved") — Lineage / Policy / Credentials / PII panels that render "not yet emitted" until producers land.

THE CANONICAL TREE (every detail view is built on it, parallel trees FOLD onto it by key): Session(thread_id, optional Investigation envelope, backed by ConsoleWorkspace) › Run(run_id; trace root; fused by run_id to ScoreCard + forensic Span tree) › Step(step_id; reasoning + tool_call_ids) › {Reasoning | ToolCall(tc-uuid, args=shell cmd, result, exit_code)} › VfsOp(OpRecord: op/path/source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix/fingerprint/revision/is_cache) › {EffectClass+CaptureState (derived now), Cache/Latency phase (from duration_ms + Span cache_hits), Lineage edge + PolicyDecision (reserved slots)}. The Span tree (bytes_read/written, api_calls, cache_hits/misses, AUDIT/TRACE/OPERATIONAL levels) folds on by session_id+timestamp today and run_id/tool_call_id once stamped; ScoreCard hangs off the Run by run_id as an overlay; the relay StreamEvent firehose is demoted to an optional raw-events drawer.

NAVIGATION FLOW list→run→detail: Runs list (rows = one run each: prompt snippet, status, model, #steps, bytes r/w, cost, wallclock, touched-mount chips, error badge) → click a row → Replay Workspace opens at tick 0 (or at the failing tick if the run errored) with the global scrubber. The Replay Workspace IS the run detail: three time-synced panels (Reasoning/Trace tree on left, in-flight Tool Call + payloads center, reconstructed VFS World on right) over the transport bar. Clicking any node in the tree, any VfsOp in the world panel, or any point on the scrubber sets the cursor — all panels snap to that instant. A detail inspector slides over the center panel for the selected node's untruncated payloads. URL encodes /runs/:runId?t=:tick (and optionally &bp=... for breakpoints) so any tick is a permalink.

primaryScreens.name: Replay Workspace (THE screen — three-panel time-travel debugger)
primaryScreens.purpose: At any instant in the agent's life, show reasoning + in-flight tool call + reconstructed VFS/world state simultaneously, and let the developer step/play/pause/rewind through the whole run. This is where 'model mistake vs data mistake' is answered in one scrub.
primaryScreens.layout: Full-height, three vertical panels over a persistent transport bar. HEADER (40px): run_id (copyable), session, model, status pill, terminal-time rollups (steps · ops · bytes r/w · cache-hit% · tokens in/out · cost · wallclock — sourced from Span/ScoreCard, not recomputed), and a 'Frozen artifact' lock badge if completed. LEFT PANEL (380px) 'Trace': the Session›Run›Step›{Reasoning,ToolCall}›VfsOp tree rendered as a vertical waterfall (reusing RunTracePanel/StepCard). Each step shows duration bar; expanding a step reveals its reasoning text, its ToolCallRows, and — nested under each tool call — its exact VfsOps (now correctly correlated by tool_call_id, not timestamp-bucketed). The node whose [start,end] contains the cursor tick is highlighted; everything after the cursor is dimmed to ~40% opacity (you literally see the 'future' greyed out, like a debugger's not-yet-executed lines). CENTER PANEL (fluid) 'Now': the in-flight unit at the cursor — if it's a reasoning tick, the streaming thinking text up to that delta; if it's a tool call, the shell command (args) + a live-typing result up to that tick + exit_code; a latency-phase bar (model vs cache-lookup vs byte-fetch vs VFS) for the active step. A detail inspector tab here holds untruncated, copyable, searchable stdout/stderr/args/result. RIGHT PANEL (420px) 'World @ tick N': the reconstructed data plane AT THE CURSOR — a mount tree (from ConsoleWorkspace.mounts) with per-mount effect-class tags, each file annotated read/written/unread-so-far; a running overlay list of captured writes up to N; a pending-effects tally up to N (gated by Investigation.authority); and for the file touched by the current op, an inline before/after content diff (overlay vs backing) plus its fingerprint/revision and cache hit/miss. TRANSPORT BAR (bottom, 56px, spans all panels): |◀ step-back · ▶/⏸ play/pause · step-forward ▶| · speed 0.5x/1x/2x/4x · a horizontal scrubber track (ticks = events; step boundaries marked; error/policy/SoR-write ticks rendered as colored notches) with a draggable playhead · a breakpoint toggle · current tick / total · timecode.
keyComponents: GlobalScrubber (draggable playhead over event ticks, notches for breakpoint-class events, step boundaries)
TransportControls (step-back/play/pause/step-forward/speed) — wires the disabled Replay/Unwind stubs into real reverse-execution
WaterfallTree with cursor-highlight + future-dimming (RunTracePanel/StepCard with onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId FINALLY passed)
NowPanel (reasoning-or-toolcall reconstructed to tick) + LatencyPhaseBar
WorldPanel@N (mount tree + overlay-so-far + pending-effects-so-far + inline before/after content DiffView with fingerprint/revision/cache badge)
DetailInspector (untruncated copyable searchable stdout/stderr/args/result)

primaryScreens.sampleInteraction: The run errored at step 9. It opens paused on the error tick. You drag the playhead back to step 6's op: the World panel shows the op read source=ram (cache hit), fingerprint md5:9a1f… while the backing mount's HEAD revision is VersionId:7c… — a stale read. primaryScreens.name: Breakpoints & Causality (the 'rewind to where it went wrong' surface)
primaryScreens.purpose: Let the developer set conditions and let Play auto-halt at the first matching tick, then walk causality backward from a byte to the reasoning that caused it.
primaryScreens.layout: A right-docked drawer (360px) that overlays the World panel on demand, plus an always-visible breakpoint affordance on the transport bar. TOP of drawer: 'Add breakpoint' with a condition builder — predicate type dropdown (Run error · exit_code != 0 · write to effect-class [scratch/durable/system-of-record/external-effect] · capture_state == live · path matches glob · bytes > N · fingerprint/revision drift vs backing · policy DENY [reserved, shown disabled with 'not yet emitted']) + value field. MIDDLE: list of active breakpoints with on/off toggles, hit-counts, and a 'jump to next hit' arrow. BOTTOM 'Causality' section: when a VfsOp or write is selected anywhere, this shows the real initiator chain (VfsOp → its ToolCall → its Step → its Reasoning) as a clickable breadcrumb, each hop setting the cursor; plus a reserved 'data lineage' sub-block (read→write provenance) rendered as 'not yet emitted (OpenLineage emit_* unimplemented)' so the slot exists honestly. Saved breakpoint SETS are nameable and reusable across runs (Library).

BreakpointList (toggle, hit-count, jump-to-next)

primaryScreens.name: Compare Runs (side-by-side regression diff)

CENTER: the two waterfall trees aligned row-by-row; diverging steps highlighted (e.g., run B took an extra tool call, or touched a different mount). signatureInteractions: Scrub-to-reconstruct: dragging the global playhead re-renders all three panels (reasoning, in-flight tool call, AND VFS world-state) to that exact tick. The right panel literally rebuilds the filesystem/overlay/pending-effects as of step N from the VfsOp subsequence + OverlayDiff + snapshots — rrweb-style replay but over a governed data plane, which no chat-replay tool can do.

Hover-correlate / click-correlate (wiring the dead hooks): hovering a reasoning step highlights, in the World panel, exactly the bytes/files that step touched; clicking it sets the cursor there. This finally passes onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId that StepCard/RunTracePanel already accept and RunPage never wired — making 'which reasoning step caused this write?' answerable.

Breakpoint-and-play 'rewind to where it went wrong': set conditions (error, policy-deny[reserved], write-to-system-of-record, external-effect, fingerprint drift, path glob, bytes>N), press Play, and the transport auto-halts at the first matching tick with its scrubber notch lit — then step backward one event at a time to find the cause.

Jump-to-cause via real causality edges: select any VfsOp and a breadcrumb walks VfsOp→ToolCall→Step→Reasoning using the now-stamped tool_call_id, so 'caused-by' is distinguishable from 'happened-after' — true reverse-debugging instead of timestamp-window bucketing.

Ground-truth diff on every write: for the file under the cursor's op, an inline before/after content diff (overlay vs backing) with fingerprint(md5/ETag)/revision(VersionId/SHA) and a cache hit/miss badge — exposing stale-read and wrong-file data bugs output-only evaluators can't express.

Latency-phase scrub: the active step's duration decomposes into model vs cache-lookup vs byte-fetch vs VFS time (from per-op duration_ms + Span cache_hits/api_calls), so you scrub to the slow step and instantly see whether to fix the prompt, the cache, or the data layout.

Permalink-to-tick: every cursor position is a shareable URL (/runs/:id?t=:tick&bp=...) into an immutable frozen artifact — paste a link that opens the exact instant the bug occurred, with breakpoints preloaded.
leveragesMirageData: "The entire right panel and the scrubber's value proposition exist ONLY because mirage observes the data plane. (1) Data-plane span layer beneath every tool call: each ToolCall node expands into its exact VfsOps (op/path/source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix/fingerprint/revision/is_cache) — a Chrome-DevTools network waterfall over real I/O, correlated by tool_call_id rather than the model's self-reported args. Competitors (LangSmith/Langfuse/Phoenix/Helicone/OTel GenAI) stop at the tool wrapper's logged args; if the agent paraphrases or truncates, their trace is wrong and they can't know. (2) Data-correctness debugging as a first-class assertion: the scrubber + fingerprint/revision badges let you SEE 'read the wrong file' or 'pulled stale data' (md5/VersionId drift vs HEAD) at the tick it happened — a bug class output-only tools structurally cannot represent. (3) True latency attribution: the LatencyPhaseBar splits each step into model/cache-lookup/byte-fetch/VFS using per-op duration_ms + the Span layer's cache_hits/api_calls metrics; nobody else has phase-level data-layer timing. (4) Effect-class + reversibility governance on REAL writes: because mirage sees the write and the mount, breakpoints can halt on 'wrote to system-of-record' / 'irreversible external effect' tied to the causing reasoning step — not an opaque equal tool call. (5) Real time-travel over state: OverlayDiff + snapshots + fingerprints reconstruct the filesystem/overlay/pending-effects at tick N with genuine before/after content diffs, where 'session replay' elsewhere only re-renders text turns. The design also folds the forensic Span tree (the sole source of aggregated bytes_read/written, api_calls, cache_hits/misses across AUDIT/TRACE/OPERATIONAL levels) and the run_id-keyed ScoreCard onto the same spine, so reasoning, verified bytes, cost, and effect are correlated by one key — the one thing a runtime-resident viewer can do that an external SDK cannot."
fixesCurrentConsole: "Maps 1:1 to the six critiques. (1) 'Run is a verb, not a noun' → Runs is the home: a per-run_id list you can name, filter, search, open, and permalink; 'chat at an agent' moves to Live as merely one way to CREATE a run. The console stops being keyed on a single consoleStore.activeId. (2) 'Cannot review past runs' → the Replay Workspace opens any run from getSessionTrace/listSessions (already in client.ts, used by the other platform, never called by the console) and replays the immutable event log; it never nulls sessionId on open and never mints a fresh empty session (kills RunPage.tsx L51-59 behavior). (3) 'Reasoning↔data correlation built and dead' → the Replay Workspace PASSES onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId (present in StepCard.tsx:39-40 / RunTracePanel.tsx:159-161, passed by nobody) so hover/click cross-highlights reasoning↔World panel↔scrubber. (4) 'Correlation is timestamp-guessed and buggy' → we stamp tool_call_id/step_id/run_id on each CUSTOM vfs_op at emission (server.py L1406-1411 already has tc_id in scope at L1422) and return exec_node.records (already returned at L1024), then fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer — replacing correlateEvents.ts's non-breaking overlapping-window loop (L34-39) and its cross-session leak (mcp_tool_call/mock_request lacking session). Causality becomes a real edge. (5) 'Governance theater drowns signal & is fake' → the persistent pending-effects counter, Promote tab, ModeBadge, LIVE red-chrome, and typed-PROMOTE modal are removed from the debugger; effect-class/capture-state/reversibility become decorations on the spine and breakpoint conditions, surfaced only when a step writes to a non-scratch class. The admittedly-simulated promote (server.py L2746-2761 'simulated:True') is separated from review entirely — 'review' never masquerades as an irreversible commit. (6) 'No diff/scrub/search, mutable evidence' → real before/after content diff per write, a global scrubber, full-text search across reasoning/args/results/op-paths, and immutable frozen artifacts (no destructive Reset on the record); it consumes the platform's existing /api/traces Span tree (TraceDetail/SpanMetrics in types.ts, endpoints at server.py L377-459, consumed by NO UI today) instead of reinventing a weaker write-focused subset; stdout truncation (4096) and dropped stderr/fingerprint/revision/source/duration_ms are surfaced by the plumbing fixes so the inspector shows untruncated, copyable payloads."
risks: The headline VfsOp→ToolCall correlation requires the backend plumbing fix (stamp tool_call_id + source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision on the CUSTOM vfs_op at server.py L1406-1411; fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer). Until it lands, the right panel and causality breadcrumb must fall back to the buggy timestamp bucketing — so the cross-highlight could mis-attribute ops between two tool calls in one step. Ship the fix first; render a 'correlation: inferred' badge wherever the fallback is used.

Cache HITS emit no OpRecord (dispatch short-circuits before record()), so the World panel's 'served from cache' and the LatencyPhaseBar's cache-lookup segment must be derived from is_cache(source=='ram'), absence of a network op, or the Span cache_hits metric — never from the op stream alone. Mislabeling a miss as a hit would undermine the stale-read story; gate cache claims on the Span metric when present.

VFS content for the before/after diff is string-parsed ls -la/cat (brittle on spaces/sizes, text-only, no real mtime/pagination). Long or binary files will diff poorly; the DiffView must tolerate truncation and clearly mark 'preview only / binary' rather than imply a byte-exact diff. Ideally move to a structured FS read.

Persistence/scale: raw events cap at 2000 in RAM, AgentStreamState in localStorage (quota, errors swallowed), ExecutionHistory deque(100). A scrubber over a long run needs the full immutable log — the Runs catalog and Replay must standardize on arcadia_store (currently optional, degrades silently to RAM) and paginate/stream, or long runs will be truncated mid-scrub.

'Reconstruct VFS world @ tick N' is only exact for the overlay/captured-writes (which we have op-by-op); the pre-run backing state of WRITTEN mounts is pinned at stand-up and not re-derivable per-tick (StatePage already flags this as a deferred Replay feature). The World panel must label backing as 'pinned at stand-up' and only claim tick-accuracy for reads-so-far + overlay, not the full backing tree.

tool_name is always 'exec' with a raw shell string (bespoke OpenAI EXEC loop, not mirage's structured backends), so read/write/external can't be classified at the tool-call level — all effect/kind classification must come from the VfsOp/effect-class layer. If a command's effect isn't reflected in any OpRecord, the breakpoint/effect tagging will miss it.

ScoreCard↔run join is convention (RunArtifacts.session_id == session), not an enforced FK; evals are produced out-of-band and the platform never triggers a sweep. The overlay must degrade to an honest 'no eval joined' empty state and not imply a guaranteed match, or users will mistake a missing scorecard for a passing run.

Reserved moat panels (lineage/policy/credential/PII) risk looking like vaporware if over-prominent. Keep them visibly 'not yet emitted', behind the Moat nav and reserved sub-blocks, so the IA doesn't churn when producers land but the debugger never appears to fake provenance/policy data.

name: Mirage Workbench
thesis: Mirage Workbench treats a Run as a first-class, immutable, permalinkable object — and makes COMPARISON its spine. A developer lands in a searchable Run Library (every past interaction, filterable by prompt text, status, error, model, cost, and — uniquely — touched mount), opens any run into a frozen waterfall built on Session›Run›Step›ToolCall›VfsOp, and at any moment pins it and diffs it against another run or against a baseline. Diff is not a feature bolted on; it is the second monitor. Because mirage observed the real I/O at the source chokepoint (OpRecord: exact path, bytes, source, cache hit, fingerprint/revision), the diff can show what no transcript-based tool can: "v2 read customers_2024.csv (ETag abc) where v1 read customers_2023.csv (ETag def)" — a data regression invisible to LangSmith/Langfuse, which only diff model-reported args. Every debugging session can be frozen into a saved Investigation (pinned runs + annotations + the exact step permalinks), turning ad-hoc spelunking into durable, shareable regression evidence. It wins for debugging agents because it answers the two questions the current console structurally cannot — "which step touched this byte?" and "what changed between the good run and the bad one?" — and it answers the second with verified ground truth rather than the model's self-report.
paradigm: Run Diff & Investigation Workbench — a notebook + git-diff for agent runs. The organizing metaphor is version control over executions: list, search, open, pin, diff (left/right), annotate, and branch/re-run from a step. Reviewing a past interaction is the default mode; "chat at an agent" is demoted to one of several ways to mint a new run. Every screen is built to scale to hundreds of runs and to make two runs comparable on three axes at once — reasoning path, data touched, and cost — all hung off one canonical spine.
informationArchitecture:
TOP-LEVEL NAV (left rail, replaces the five workspace-scoped tabs that today all hang off a single consoleStore.activeId): (1) Runs — the library + diff + run detail; the home of the product. (2) Investigations — saved debugging sessions (pinned runs + notes + permalinks), backed by the existing investigations table + InvestigationMeta. (3) Effects & State — the governance/time-travel surface (overlay diff, pending effects, scrubber), reached contextually from a run but also listable. (4) Evaluations — sweep/ScoreCard browser that links INTO runs by run_id. (5) Raw Feed — the relay StreamEvent firehose, explicitly secondary. A persistent top bar holds global search and a "Compare" tray showing currently-pinned runs (0–2).

THE OBJECT HIERARCHY AS NAVIGATED (the one spine, folded): Run Library (list of Runs grouped under Sessions) → click a row → Run Detail (the waterfall: Run ▸ Step ▸ {Reasoning | ToolCall} ▸ VfsOp, with the Span tree, ScoreCard, and relay events folded onto it by key) → click any node → Inspector panel (right) shows that node's payload. From a VfsOp you can jump UP ("which step caused this?") via tool_call_id→step_id→run_id, and from a Step you can jump DOWN to the exact bytes it touched (the dead onSelectStep/highlightedStepId hooks, finally wired). From Run Detail: Pin (adds to Compare tray) → when two are pinned, "Diff" opens Run Diff (split waterfall). From any node: "Permalink" yields /console/runs/:runId#step-:stepId (or #op-:opIdx), stable and immutable. "Save to Investigation" snapshots the current pins + selection + a note.

HOW A USER MOVES list → run → detail: Runs list rows are Run summaries (prompt preview, status, model, wall, cost, op count, touched-mount chips) nested under collapsible Session headers (session_id == thread_id, optionally carrying an Investigation envelope). Selecting a row routes to Run Detail (loaded via getSessionTrace(session_id) replayed through aguiEventReducer, joined to its Span trace via getTrace + its ScoreCard via getScorecard when present). The waterfall is navigation; the right Inspector is detail — the convergent LangSmith/Phoenix/DevTools pattern, here with a verified-bytes bottom layer. Crucially, opening a run NEVER mints or resets a session (the RunPage useEffect[activeId]→setSessionId(null) bug is deleted); review is pure read.

primaryScreens.layout: Top: a sticky Run header — prompt, status, model, and rollup chips (steps · tool calls · ops · bytes r/w · cache-hit% · tokens in/out · cost · wall), a streaming/frozen indicator, and actions (Pin, Permalink, Save to Investigation, Re-run from step…, Export). Body is a 3-pane split. LEFT (waterfall, ~58%): a time-proportioned waterfall of the spine. Row 1 = Run. Indented = Steps (reuse StepCard, now driven by REAL tool_call_id→VfsOp edges, not correlateEvents timestamp buckets). Under each step: a Reasoning sublane and one bar per ToolCall (the exec boundary). Under each ToolCall: child VfsOp rows — the differentiating layer — each bar split into latency PHASES (model→dispatch | cache-lookup | byte-fetch) using duration_ms + Span cache metrics, colored by mount, with a cache hit/miss pip and a tiny effect-class tag on writes. signatureInteractions: Pin-and-Diff: star any two runs into the Compare tray and open a synchronized dual-waterfall with git-style gutters; flip between Reasoning / Tool calls / Data touched / Cost & gates without losing alignment. This is the product's heartbeat — review by comparison.

Jump-to-cause (down) and Jump-to-cause (up): click a reasoning Step and its real VfsOps glow in place; from any VfsOp, a 'caused by' breadcrumb walks tool_call_id→step_id→run_id back to the reasoning that triggered it — causality, not chronology, because the edge is now stamped at emission rather than guessed by timestamp window.

Data-touched diff with fingerprint/revision deltas: the diff that no transcript tool can do — 'right read customers_2024.csv (ETag abc) where left read customers_2023.csv (ETag def)' — turning silent stale-data and wrong-file bugs into a one-glance red/green row.

State scrub with real content diff: drag a single cursor to reconstruct the VFS/overlay/pending-effects at step N and see the actual before/after text of any captured write, then jump to the step that caused it — time-travel over the data plane, not just the chat transcript.

Permalink to one exact step/op: every node yields a stable /console/runs/:runId#op-:idx URL into an immutable, frozen artifact, so a teammate opens your finding cold — and the run is never reset out from under you (the eager session-mint/null-on-switch bug is gone).
leveragesMirageData: Mirage sits between reasoning and the data plane, so it records ground truth (OpRecord: exact path, bytes, source, cache hit, duration_ms, fingerprint/revision) instead of trusting model-reported args. The Workbench exploits the reasoning↔data correlation that only mirage has in four places competitors cannot copy: (1) The waterfall's bottom layer is verified VfsOps under each ToolCall, attached by the now-populated tool_call_id (return exec_node.records, stamp tool_call_id/step_id/run_id at the CUSTOM vfs_op emission, fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer) — collapsing the three incompatible correlation schemes and killing the buggy non-breaking timestamp loop in correlateEvents.ts. (2) Run Diff's 'Data touched' mode diffs the real VfsOp set by path+op with fingerprint(ETag/md5)/revision(VersionId/SHA) deltas — expressing 'read the wrong/stale file,' a bug class output-only evaluators structurally cannot represent. (3) Per-op latency phase decomposition (model vs cache-lookup vs byte-fetch) from duration_ms + the Span layer's cache_hits/api_calls/bytes metrics — data-layer phase timing nobody else has; cache HITS (which emit no OpRecord) are reconstructed honestly from is_cache(source=='ram'), the absence of a network op, and the Span cache_hits metric, and labeled as derived. (4) Effects & State flags writes to system-of-record / irreversible external effects by the observed mount, tied to the causing step, with a real overlay-vs-backing content diff and a step scrubber — because mirage saw the write and the mount, not an opaque tool call. The Span tree (only place bytes_read/written/api_calls/cache metrics aggregate) and the ScoreCard fold onto the same spine by session_id+timestamp now and run_id once stamped, so reasoning, I/O, cost, and effect are correlated on one key.
fixesCurrentConsole: Maps one-to-one onto the six critiqued failures. (1) 'Run is a verb' → Run/Trace becomes a first-class, listable, filterable, permalinkable noun in the Run Library; the single consoleStore.activeId model is replaced by URL-routed run IDs. (2) 'Cannot review past runs' → the Library calls the already-existing listSessions()/getSessionTrace() (used by the other platform, never by the console) and replays them; opening a run is pure read and NEVER mints or nulls a session, deleting the RunPage useEffect[activeId]→setSessionId(null) and eager createConsoleSession bug. (3) 'Reasoning↔data correlation built and dead' → the onSelectStep/onHoverStep/highlightedStepId hooks that RunPage passes to nobody are wired end-to-end so clicking a step highlights the bytes it touched. (4) 'Correlation timestamp-guessed and buggy' → replaced by real tool_call_id→VfsOp edges stamped at emission (exec_node.records), removing the non-breaking last-match loop and the cross-session leak from session-less mcp_tool_call/mock_request; inferred-only data is labeled. (5) 'Governance theater drowns the signal, and it's fake' → the persistent pending-effects counter / Promote tab / typed-PROMOTE modal are removed from the debugging path; effect class/capture state/reversibility become decorations surfaced contextually in Effects & State, review is separated from commit, and simulated promote is honestly labeled rather than dressed as guarded. (6) 'No diff, no scrub, no search, mutable evidence' → Run Diff (split waterfall, three axes), the state scrubber with real before/after content diff, full-text + faceted search including cross-run 'touched mount,' immutable frozen run artifacts (destructive Reset removed from review), and first-class reuse of the platform's existing Span tree (/api/traces, listTraces/getTrace) and ScoreCard infra instead of a weaker write-focused reinvention.
risks: The exact VfsOp→ToolCall correlation is the linchpin and requires backend plumbing (return exec_node.records; stamp tool_call_id/step_id/run_id at CUSTOM vfs_op emission, server.py ~L1401-1412; fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer, ~L173-179). Until it lands the waterfall must fall back to labeled timestamp-window correlation, and that fallback must be visibly marked 'inferred' so we don't repeat the current false-certainty bug.

ScoreCard join is by convention (RunArtifacts.session_id == session id), with no enforced FK from scorecards.run_id and no in-platform trigger to run a sweep — so the Evaluation overlay may be empty or mismatched for live runs until the FK and a trigger are wired; the UI must degrade to 'no eval for this run' gracefully.

The forensic Span tree is currently a 20-command demo with agent_id='demo-agent' and no real session join; the latency-phase and metric rollups depend on wiring real session_id/run_id into TracingWorkspace spans. Until then, phase decomposition is partly derived/estimated and must be labeled as such.

Cache HITS emit no telemetry (dispatch short-circuits before record()), so 'served from cache' is inferred from is_cache/absence-of-network-op/Span cache_hits — a real risk of over- or under-counting; show it as derived, never as a logged op.

Persistence and scale: today raw events cap at 2000 in RAM, AgentStreamState lives in localStorage (quota risk, silently swallowed), ExecutionHistory is a bounded deque(100). A review-at-scale tool MUST standardize on the arcadia_store and paginate/stream; if it silently degrades to RAM the Library and search become lossy.

Content diff and VFS preview rely on string-parsed ls -la/cat (brittle on spaces/sizes, text-only, no real mtime/pagination); large or binary writes may diff poorly until a structured FS read replaces the parsing.

tool_name is always 'exec' with a raw shell-string arg (bespoke OpenAI EXEC loop, not mirage's structured backends), so read/write/external can't be classified at the tool-call level — all effect classification must come from the VfsOp/effect-class layer, and the effect-class map itself is a heuristic, not a mirage concept (must be labeled as inferred).

Lineage/provenance, policy/ACL/budget decisions, credential lifecycle, and PII findings have no real producers (emit_* and broker/catalog methods are NotImplementedError); these slots must render honest 'not yet emitted' placeholders and never fabricate edges, at the cost of looking incomplete in demos.

Risk of feature sprawl: with Library, Run Detail, Diff, Effects & State, Eval overlay, and Investigations, the diff/compare spine must stay the obvious default or the product drifts back toward a tab pile; the Compare tray and pin affordance need to be omnipresent and cheap.
